newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: Manila shares ended in negative territory on Monday, falling 37.73 points, or 1.27 percent, to 2,935.86 as an early technical rally induced local investors to resort to profit taking, traders said.
"Any rally was seen as an opportunity to profit take or cut losses," said Teresa Lee, trader at Lippo Securities.

The market opened strongly with the index reaching a high of 2,987.96 points but it slid on profit-taking. The market was volatile and the decline in the index was exacerbated by a fall in Ayala Land B shares at midsession by one peso to 26.
Wall Street's gains on Friday failed to sustain the index's initial uptick, outweighed by the drop in blue chips, traders added.
Aside from Ayala, PLDT fell by 15 pesos to 1,500 pesos a share and Petron dropped by 10 centavos to 9.10 pesos a share.
In the absence of foreign investors' support on blue chips, secondary issues such as Zeus Holdings and Crown Equities recorded gains enticing punters.
Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn said he is still upbeat the market will recover within the week once it tests the 2,900 points support level.
